record_type_quote: This article reports a pre-registered, higher-power replication of that study (using twice the sample size and changing from a between- to a within-participants manipulation).

targets.authors: Proverbio A, Massetti G, Rizzi E, Zani A.
targets.title: Skilled musicians are not subject to the McGurk effect.
targets.evidence_quote: Proverbio and colleagues [ 2 ] argue that the McGurk effect is absent in highly trained musicians. For these reasons, it is valuable to conduct a close replication of this study to assess whether skilled musicians really are not subject to the McGurk effect.
targets.outcome_quote: Contrary to the original study's conclusion, we find that musicians do show a large and statistically significant McGurk effect and that their effect is no smaller than that of non-musicians.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The new-sample study contradicts the original central claim of absent/reduced McGurk susceptibility in musicians. Discussion distinguishes compatibility with noisy original numerical results from contradiction of the original substantive conclusions.
